thread:
Priya (support): Heads-up — ACME (tenant acme-42) just escalated: p99 for /v1/generate jumped ~6x since 08:10 UTC, mostly for tiny prompts (<=8 tokens). Customer seeing 2-3x p95 too. They reported a few 504s. Pls triage.
Miguel (oncall eng-sre): Thanks. Can you paste the route + model + last deploy tag and a dashboard link? Any auth/billing errors?
Priya (support): route: /v1/generate, model: gptx-8k-quant-v2, deploy tag: release-2026-03-16-2. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/acme-42/requests?range=30m. No auth/billing errors in logs.
Miguel (oncall eng-sre): Looking at traces — lots of requests are tiny and arrive bursty. Batcher hold times spike near upper bound.
Sara (eng-runtime): FYI we rolled adaptive coalesce in the regional pool last night. Config excerpt from rollout:
```
batching:
  strategy: adaptive_coalesce
  min_wait_ms: 8
  max_hold_ms: 120
  min_batch_size: 1
  max_batch_size_tokens: 4096
  hold_backoff_ratio: 0.6
```
Mike (eng-sre): From infra metrics (last 20m): p99 jumped from ~180ms -> 1.1s for that route. CPU on worker pods is fine, but queue_wait_ms distribution shows a heavy tail with values clustering at ~110-120ms. I can share flamegraphs if helpful.
Jess (support): Customer observed 504 gateway timeouts and a few 500s with "batch queue full" in service log. They sent sample request ids: r_8a7c, r_8a8f.
deploy-bot: New rollout applied to region-ap-south at 2026-03-16T23:50Z (strategy: rolling).
Miguel (oncall eng-sre): Hypothesis: adaptive_coalesce is increasing wait time to pack batches when incoming inter-arrival is bursty + many tiny payloads -> tail latency spike. Repro steps: run a tight fanout of tiny requests to the route with concurrency to mimic ACME spike. Example:
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"input":"hi","max_tokens":6}' &
done; wait
```
Sara (eng-runtime): Agreed. Quick mitigation options:
- Option A (fast): disable adaptive_coalesce for the affected pool (instant config flip)
- Option B (moderate): lower max_hold_ms -> 40ms and set min_wait_ms=4, min_batch_size=2 (less pack, lower tail)
- Option C (slower): per-tenant routing to a small-request-optimized pool with greedy batching.
Mike (eng-sre): Can run Option B as a canary in region (patch config map, rollout 10% pods). Low risk. Expected p99 drop but some throughput inefficiency.
Priya (support): Customer asks for ETA and risk. They prefer minimal impact to success rate.
Sara (eng-runtime): ETA for canary config change: ~12min to patch and observe. Risk: ~10-15% token cost delta for those requests, but should eliminate 504s. I'll prepare the k8s patch:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  batching.strategy: adaptive_coalesce
  batching.min_wait_ms: "4"
  batching.max_hold_ms: "40"
  batching.min_batch_size: "2"
```
Mike (eng-sre): I'll run canary and monitor routes + SLOs. Will revert if error rate increases.
(10 minutes later)
Mike (eng-sre): Canary applied to 2 pods in region. Preliminary metrics: p99 for /v1/generate dropped from 1.1s -> ~220ms for tiny prompts, p95 back near baseline. No increase in 5xx.
Priya (support): Customer confirmed they see immediate improvement, 504s stopped. :tada: They still care about cost but ok for now.
Sara (eng-runtime): I'll push a progressive rollout to 50% after another 20m of clean signals, and schedule a follow-up to evaluate long-term config. Action items:
- Sara: progressive rollout & post-mortem notes (owner)
- Mike: run synthetic small-prompt churn tests and add guardrails to auto-fallback when p99>500ms
- Priya/Jess: update customer with RCA + mitigation and timeline for follow-up
Miguel (oncall eng-sre): Also adding a telemetry alarm to detect "small-payload p99 > 400ms" for routes with >30% tiny requests.
Jess (support): Customer thanked team. Closing temporary escalation; will reopen if any regression. :white_check_mark:
